Well, there are three demographics for LoL E-Sports (and anything else, ever):

* Casuals

* Cores

* Hardcores

Casuals sure as heck don't want to see things like the laneswap meta; they want to see action and excitement, loads of back and forth interactions... And they definitely want what they see to look like what they play.

Hardcores just want to see the best of the best do their thing - they want to see optimal play. Now, here, the thing is that you can change what optimal play is... If in the PoV of the Hardcores laneswaping is the optimal strategy, they will like it and appreciate when it is done well, as well how it contrasts and interacts with other strategies... 

See, Casuals just want to be entertained.

Hardcores are about "appreciating the skill and strategy" - they derive their viewing enjoyment out of that and in comparison to the Casuals, their viewing experience is both more in-depth and demanding.

However... Neither of these two demographics *truly* matter.

Casuals care more about the game itself than LoL E-Sports, whereas Hardcores will tolerate just about anything; further, as with any fanbase, their numbers reflect this - the Casuals are by far the most numerous while the Hardcores are the "niche".

So this is where the Cores come in: They are regular, dependent and "steady" in the viewing habits, balanced in their taste and, obviously, take the middle ground in terms of population. They care a lot and have decent understanding of depth (in contrast to Casuals) while being more easy going and less critical (in contrast to Hardcores).

Basically, they are "the meat" of the viewerbase, making them the most important; further, they are (as I implied) neither here nor there in terms of stylistic preferences and, importantly, what they derive enjoyment from.

Do they appreciate a good ol' fast-paced, back-and-forth bloodbath?

Yes.

Do they appreciate skillful play and intelligent teamwide strategy? 

Yes.

What "ratio" is optimal for them (obviously on average)? 

I'd say 70:30, 60:40 at the lowest.

So, seeing strategy is nice and all - but if the game is slow, plodding, formulaic, filled with little action (and little consequences), as well as one-sided... It just won't work.

That is the case of current Pro LoL (and has been for a while)... Generally slow, formulaic, repetitive; the action is in relatively low amounts or just isn't satisfying; the strategy on display is too obtuse and isn't "visible" enough, while often being more about set-ups and avoiding interactions than combat-centric proactive play.

Finally, oh boy, is it snowbally - which is why whenever there is a close and "bloody" match, every screams "clown fiesta"... Because, indeed, that is basically the only way you can get a close, back-and-forth game: loads of unforced errors.

And the reasons I mentioned earlier are why whenever people scream *that*, others argue back that "they don't care, they still enjoyed it".

Which brings me back to my point: People prefer more "direct" executions of tactics and macro-strategy, with it being combat-centric and "visible", not preparation-centric and obtuse. 

This naturally leads into more *action and kills* and what is general considered "proactive play" while nonetheless containing strategy.

However, at the end of the day, that is what it is all about: Action & combat, usually at a fast pace (but not constantly so) in an even, back-and-forth flow, all leading to a climactic finale - and the strategy employed and *on display* is supposed to facilitate that directly, nothing more or less... And *not* be about avoiding combat and things like "winning via attrition".

Now, after reading all of this, you can say: "dude, sure, fine and dandy, but where is your empirical evidence that the average viewer has such tastes and stylistic preferences?".

Well, I don't have any - just logic.

However, I wholeheartedly believe in it; I think you can take 10/100/1000 regular LoL E-Sports viewers (so, the Cores) and show them Pro LoL gameplay on an experimental test patch aimed to achieve the gameplay style I am talking about and 9/10 would prefer it.
